source.title: From Verification Failures to ReusableGuidance for Coding Agents

quote_checks.quote: We investigate how expert-curated procedures connect language semantics, specifications, proof extensions, and adequacy checks.
quote_checks.node_text: DafnyBench evaluates generation of missing proof hints ( Loughridge et al., 2024 ) , and AutoVerus organizes proof generation, refinement, and repair ( Yang et al., 2025 ) . Clover checks consistency among code, descriptions, and formal annotations ( Sun et al., 2024 ) . Reflexion retains textual reflections on feedback for subsequent attempts ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) . We investigate how expert-curated procedures connect language semantics, specifications, proof extensions, and adequacy checks.

quote_checks.quote: Experts inspected failures, diagnosed their causes, wrote procedures with applicability conditions, attached checking examples, and retained the changes in versioned resources.
quote_checks.node_text: The initial HumanEval effort alternated proof attempts with expert diagnosis and repair. The first pass established language support and verification practices. The second pass organized generation, checking, and audit into a staged campaign. Experts inspected failures, diagnosed their causes, wrote procedures with applicability conditions, attached checking examples, and retained the changes in versioned resources. Semantic discrepancies produced revised language rules and tests that exposed the errors. Recurring proof failures produced procedures for subsequent agents. Figure 1 separates this curation process from work on an individual task.

quote_checks.quote: Its effect on later tasks is unmeasured.
quote_checks.node_text: The split_words repair provides a traceable curation example. Its original predicate recognized four of CPython’s 29 whitespace code points. The repair pins CPython and Unicode versions, implements all 29 members, and checks the table across every code point. The new kit entry requires a pinned library reference, complete finite-domain comparisons, boundary tests, and replays of affected consumers. The artifact links this instruction to the predicate change and independent checks in kit/revisions/2026-09-24/ . Appendix A.1 records the repair evidence. The example records the instruction’s provenance and checking procedure. Its effect on later tasks is unmeasured.

quote_checks.quote: Kit instead adds a fixed historical core of procedures
quote_checks.node_text: We test whether the kit’s procedures improve acceptance beyond complete rules and generic advice on all 31 original programs under swapped semantics. Each program receives one attempt in each of three arms. Rules supplies the complete acceptance requirements. Generic adds advice about planning, checking, and revision. Kit instead adds a fixed historical core of procedures for scope, invariant derivation, circularity matching, residual inspection, and non-vacuity. The latter two additions each contain 2,145 tokens under the same named tokenizer. Every excerpt is supplied at the start. The arms share programs, semantics, mathematical vocabulary, checks, and time limits.

quote_checks.quote: The present comparisons use a fixed historical core on existing programs whose prior exposure to kit editors is unknown.
quote_checks.node_text: The controlled experiments evaluate guidance beyond complete task rules and generic advice. Luna’s kit count is higher and DeepSeek’s is lower, with every paired interval spanning zero. These measurements give a reproducible baseline for improving procedure selection. The coverage traces and DeepSeek’s more frequent kit-arm budget stops suggest two concrete experiments. Remove individual procedures to identify which instructions help preserve the input domain, and compare fixed excerpts with adaptive loading under several budgets. Selecting a new task family after freezing the resources would measure transfer with a clear exposure boundary. The present comparisons use a fixed historical core on existing programs whose prior exposure to kit editors is unknown.

source.title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents

quote_checks.quote: In the procedures/ directory there are textual or executable sequences of actions which the agent is able to reuse and modify during later interactions.
quote_checks.node_text: Procedural memory consists of methods that can be reused. In the procedures/ directory there are textual or executable sequences of actions which the agent is able to reuse and modify during later interactions. Experience is converted into these kinds of knowledge and skill through periodic consolidation ( Kumaran et al., 2016 ) . The agent can add to, correct or reorganize these procedures as new evidence becomes available, the underlying episodic records staying unaltered.

quote_checks.quote: the agent is able to convert a sequence of actions into a textual or executable procedure and then modify it as a result of the changes revealed by later attempts.
quote_checks.node_text: Procedural updates record effective methods of acting; the agent is able to convert a sequence of actions into a textual or executable procedure and then modify it as a result of the changes revealed by later attempts. Working-memory updates link the knowledge that has been accumulated to the current task by having the agent revise the file working.md to show the completed subgoals, any changes to the plan, and the questions that remain unanswered. The agent decides which of these updates to make on the basis of the evidence available and the role of each memory, and the resulting documents and procedures stay accessible during future interactions.

quote_checks.quote: it is the agent itself that decides which behaviours to keep and when to reuse them.
quote_checks.node_text: We look into whether long-term memory allows agents to enhance their future behaviour by turning experience from interactions into reusable procedures. In this context, self-improvement means adapting as a result of the memory accumulated in MFM. MFM includes the facilities needed to store, modify, and carry out procedures written by the agent, and it is the agent itself that decides which behaviours to keep and when to reuse them. We do not specify the resulting skill library and do not require a fixed number of skills for each run. The analysis presented in this section includes observations of skill creation and reuse over different trajectories, an ablation study of the agent-written procedures, and a controlled study of the number of steps required to solve new tasks with or without reusing the agent-written procedures.

quote_checks.quote: The agent also disabled one inherited procedure, level_step , having traced the previous death in the lava back to this procedure’s release of the sneak key.
quote_checks.node_text: From experience to reusable behaviour. The trajectories show how agents convert their experience of interaction into permanent action routines. In a run of GPT-6-Astra Dragon, after manually cutting a descending staircase (steps 5,068 to 5,249), the agent created the procedure cut_step , which is parameterised by heading and cuts one step while advancing ( ); it then invoked this procedure 60 times, once for each of the four cardinal headings. A second procedure, quarry_north_pair , extracts the upper and lower block from the wall in front and gathers the dropped items ( ); the 27th time it was called, at step 17,462, it broke the first diamond ore block. Reuse also carries over from one life to another. The procedure bridge_north , which places one floor block while sneaking and takes the target cell as input ( ), was written in the previous life after the agent had manually placed two blocks over the lava and was then called three times in that same life. In this life the agent called it nine times between steps 19,261 and 20,103, using inputs ranging from (x=-3037, y=29, z=-5657) to (x=-3037, y=33, z=-5665) . Each invocation placed one cobblestone block and left the agent’s health unchanged, and the bridge ended up reaching the lava pool where mining of obsidian took place at step 20,736. The agent also disabled one inherited procedure, level_step , having traced the previous death in the lava back to this procedure’s release of the sneak key.

quote_checks.quote: Revision targets the natural-language instructions and behavioral specifications in SKILL.md , the implementation code of bundled executable scripts, or both.
quote_checks.node_text:
Each SkillScriptBench task provides an existing executable Agent Skill package S S and
a natural-language request q q describing the required functionality or a failure
to be resolved. Revision targets the natural-language instructions and behavioral
specifications in SKILL.md , the implementation code of bundled executable
scripts, or both. A method returns a candidate package S ′ S^{\prime} whose executable
behavior satisfies q q and whose documentation consistently describes that
behavior, while preserving behavior outside the requested scope.

quote_checks.quote: Success requires passing all applicable tests in both categories.
quote_checks.node_text:
We evaluate functional correctness and documentation–script consistency.
Behavioral tests check the requested
functionality and preservation of correct behavior, while documentation-driven
tests execute task-relevant invocations and workflows from SKILL.md against the revised scripts. Success requires passing all applicable tests
in both categories.

quote_checks.quote: Edits leave source text outside the selected spans unchanged and are accepted only if the resulting scripts pass syntax and applicable interface-preservation checks.
quote_checks.node_text:
The revision model uses the repair targets, caller–helper context, and
preservation constraints in ℛ \mathcal{R} to generate node-level script
replacements for each package version. Edits leave source text outside the
selected spans unchanged and are accepted only if the resulting scripts pass
syntax and applicable interface-preservation checks. Assembly uses S ~ \widetilde{S} as its base, retaining its validated edits and incorporating
compatible edits from S S through unique source matching.
The model then aligns documented invocations and operational instructions with
the maintenance request q q and the resulting scripts, correcting identified
inconsistencies through localized Markdown edits supported by script evidence.
Appendices A.3 and A.4 detail
the feedback representation, edit validation, and package assembly rules.

quote_checks.quote: A failure reported by the verifier or its executed checks triggers the generator to revise SKILL.md and scripts using the diagnosis and check results.
quote_checks.node_text:
We adapt CoEvoSkills ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) to maintenance-request-driven
revision of executable Skill packages. An independent surrogate verifier
assesses the package against the request and produces requirement-linked checks
and a diagnosis. A failure reported by the verifier or its executed checks
triggers the generator to revise SKILL.md and scripts using the
diagnosis and check results. To obtain CoEvoSkills + AST, we use the returned
package as the initial revision S ~ \widetilde{S} and apply AST-Guided Skill
Revision to ( q , S , S ~ ) (q,S,\widetilde{S}) .

quote_checks.quote: reliability in long-horizon downstream Agent workflows remains to be evaluated.
quote_checks.node_text:
The In-the-Wild track is predominantly Python, and both tracks use constructed
faults to evaluate package maintenance. Broader language coverage and tasks
derived from naturally occurring failures would help assess generalization
to the wider Skill ecosystem. Our evaluation measures package-level correctness
and documentation–script consistency; reliability in long-horizon downstream
Agent workflows remains to be evaluated.

quote_checks.quote: The agent learns only from this context, as its weights stay fixed.
quote_checks.node_text: Outer loop: structural revision. Each round starts with one prompt to the agent (Sec. C.2 ). The prompt contains the task request, scene context, and verifier 𝒞 \mathcal{C} , the current best program with its rollout feedback, and the skill library ℋ \mathcal{H} . The agent learns only from this context, as its weights stay fixed. It proposes several new programs. A validator discards programs that break the code rules, such as reading an undeclared feature, before any rollout. Keeping the current best in context encourages targeted repairs when a strategy is close, while allowing new structures when it is not.

quote_checks.node_text: Skill library. The skill library is a text document for summarizing tasks, placed in the agent’s prompt every round. Each entry records a completed task: its scene, task text, verifier with the pass rate of each criterion, and the selected program with its tuned constants. With these entries in context, the agent can compose or adapt established programs instead of evolving from scratch.
